sections.h2: Which Laurel County offices touch a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Three offices in and around London split the job. One values the property, one collects the money, and one inherits whatever stays unpaid. Calling the wrong one costs a seller time, so here is who does what.

  • Property Valuation Administrator (PVA): Room 127 at 101 S. Main St. Call (606) 864-2889. The office closes at 4:30 Monday through Friday, and its website runs parcel searches by street address, owner name or parcel number.
  • Sheriff: 1380 East Hwy 192. Call 606-864-6600. Counter service ends at 4:00 on weekdays, and Saturday and Sunday are closed.
  • County Clerk: Room 203 at the same Main Street address, phone (606) 864-5158. The clerk receives delinquent bills and runs the sale of the liens.

The rate differs by taxing district, so get the figure for your own parcel from the sheriff or the PVA.

sections.h2: What should an owner know about Laurel County itself?
sections.html:
The state cut Laurel County out of four older counties in December 1825, and it now covers about 434 square miles of land. London is the seat. Corbin lies mostly across the border in Whitley County. Its borders take in sections of the Daniel Boone National Forest and Laurel River Lake. History buffs know it for the Civil War fight at Wildcat Mountain, and visitors for the first Kentucky Fried Chicken cafe north of Corbin and the World Chicken Festival in London.

  • Population: an estimated 63,746 in July 2025, up from 62,613 in 2020 and 58,849 in 2010, with a 2020 density of 144 residents per square mile.
  • Older and disabled residents: 19.1 percent of people are 65 or above, and 16.6 percent of those under 65 report a disability, the two groups the homestead exemption below serves.
  • Housing: 27,063 units, 23,996 households, 71.6 percent owned by their occupants.
  • Middle home value $159,500. Owners with a mortgage carry median monthly costs of $1,239, and owners without one report $382.
  • The Census Bureau counted 21 building permits for the county in 2025.
  • Jobs: 1,272 employer establishments and 23,992 workers in 2023, with retail sales near $1.68 billion in 2022.
  • Money and movement: median household income of $57,771, a 22.6 minute average commute, and 2.57 people per household.

sections.h2: What are the Laurel County payment dates and penalties?
sections.html:
The assessment date is New Year's Day, and the tax for that year is due at the sheriff's office before December 31 ends. KRS 134.015 turns the calendar into money.

  • Settle in full by November 1 and 2 percent comes off.
  • Between November 2 and December 31 the full printed amount is owed.
  • January adds 5 percent on top.
  • February and later add 10 percent.

If bills are late getting out, the state can swap in a shifted timetable with a discount month followed by a face-value month. The sheriff's page lists three routes: walk in, mail a check, or leave one in the box on the building's front. Cards work at the office only. Cash does not belong in either, and a mailed receipt needs an envelope you have addressed and stamped.

sections.h2: How can a Laurel County owner contest a value?
sections.html:
Start by talking to the PVA or a deputy, since the local board will not hear an owner who skipped that step. The real property roll opens to the public on the first Monday in May for thirteen days, Saturdays included. The clerk's office takes the written appeal, and the cutoff is closing time on the next workday after viewing wraps up.

The board convenes about a month after viewing ends. Bring proof such as sales of similar houses, an insurance policy, what the building cost, or a description of the lot. Appeals that arrive without documents get denied, and a no-show at the hearing forfeits any later claim to the Kentucky Claims Commission. Bills that print mid-dispute use the owner's number, and a supplemental bill follows if the board's value comes out higher.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for homestead relief in Laurel County?
sections.html:
The state subtracts $49,100 from the assessment in the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. A house assessed at $200,000 ends up taxable at $150,900. Eligible owners are at least 65 years old or classified as totally disabled. With so many older residents, a share of Laurel County sellers may have it on file already.

Applications are filed at the PVA's Room 127 office, along with documents showing age or disability. A claim based on disability is renewed yearly. Two groups skip the renewal: veterans with a service connected disability, and owners that Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has ruled permanently and totally disabled. Ask the PVA how the exemption is treated after the house is sold.

sections.h2: What does a delinquent Laurel County tax bill turn into?
sections.html:
On April 15 the sheriff's collection season ends. Open bills pass to the clerk, who records a lien and relabels each one a certificate of delinquency. A 1 percent monthly interest charge starts, and even a few days into a month counts as the whole month. The state's sample bill is $1,000. By the handoff it is $1,254, assuming a 4 percent sheriff commission, and each later step adds interest and commissions for the clerk and county attorney.

Cost of a $1,000 Kentucky tax bill the longer it sits at the clerk (Department of Revenue samples; the last column is the gain over the handoff total)
Payment pointTotalGain
Handoff from sheriff$1,254.00none
Inside five business days$1,387.79$133.79
Following the first county attorney letter$1,611.30$357.30

The county attorney mails a first notice within 30 days of the transfer and a second within 60 days, and the second names the sale date. The sale itself falls between 90 and 135 days after the transfer, and a third party who buys the certificate may tack on substantial fees. The Laurel County Clerk's notice for the 2026 sale had outside buyers registering August 17 through August 31 with a deposit of 25 percent of their list value, and that registration window is over. The same notice set the 2026 sale lottery for September 9 at 9:00 a.m. in the clerk's Delinquent Tax Department, also past. KRS 134.015 lets that lien last eleven years, whoever holds title.

sections.h2: What tax steps should a Laurel County seller finish before listing?
sections.html:
• Get a statement from the sheriff showing this year's bill and any older year still open.
  • Ask the clerk's delinquent tax staff whether a certificate already exists against the parcel.
  • Check the PVA website to confirm owner name, parcel number and assessed value.
  • Use the bill search links on the sheriff's website to pull the parcel's tax history, and bring the printout to the listing appointment.
  • If you hold the homestead exemption, ask the PVA what happens to it at the sale.
  • Write the split of the current year's bill into the contract so the closing agent knows each side's share.

Sellers who want to skip repairs can request a direct offer. Whatever tax is still owed gets paid from the sale proceeds.

faqs.q: Where does a Laurel County owner pay the tax bill?
faqs.a: At the sheriff's office, 1380 East Hwy 192, London. Payment is accepted at the counter with a card, by mailed check and at the drop box outside.

faqs.q: How big is the early payment discount in Laurel County?
faqs.a: Two percent, for full payment received by November 1. After that the printed amount applies through December.

faqs.q: Which office handles a disagreement over value?
faqs.a: Start with the PVA's office at (606) 864-2889, because a meeting there is required before any appeal.

faqs.q: How much does the Kentucky homestead exemption take off?
faqs.a: It removes $49,100 of assessed value for owners who qualify, and the PVA takes the application.

faqs.q: Does a tax lien stay with the property after a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. KRS 134.015 lets a delinquent tax lien run eleven years whoever owns the land, which is why a buyer's title agent looks for one.
